Balatro is one of those games that doesn’t seem like it will have enough to hook you for an hour or two much less the 200 something hours I have at this point. 

The first time I played the game my thought process went
It’s just poker solitaire? Then the jokers show up and your brain starts to adapt, Oh what’s this Tarot cards? Lucky cards? Spectral cards? 
All of a sudden tons of depth and synergy emerge and when you look up it’s been 3 hours. And the beautiful thing is that as a roguelike game every run is unique just like every game of cards is.

The first time you see the flames pop up, the first run you win, your first gold stake victory all of it becomes this beautiful obsession. I play this game constantly and watch streamers play it daily.

I don’t have a gambling problem, I have a Balatro problem.

How good are you at video poker and do you even like video poker? Ask yourself those two questions before you buy this game. Because friends, Balatro is just video poker- on steroids. I first played Balatro when they brought it to Dave The Diver, and it PISSED ME OFF so badly because I just could not get the hang of the dang game! Eventually, I grew to love it. I'm already a huge fan of video poker, (that's mostly where you'll find me in a casino) so I view this game as quite a challenge, with a huge spin and a fantastic new take on classic video poker! You get cards that multiply your hands, common, uncommon, rare, etc. It keeps the game interesting. Each phase is different. The game in itself is actually quite challenging, because you need the right combination of cards to complete your run. It really sucks when you're ALMOST there, and BAM. "Who's the Joker now?" I definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys cards, casino, or poker games. Stay away if they bore you. This is a 10/10 gem and I waited forever to purchase it. I'm so glad I finally did! I think this is the best card game out there right now, and it's a must play!

I don't think Balatro is the single best deck-building roguelike on the market, but occupying the number two slot isn't an insult to it to any degree. There's a lot to like about the game - I enjoyed the hunt of unlocking everything in the collection, getting used to my favorite builds and how to find them.

There's a conversation to be had about RNG in games like this, and by some measure, Balatro suffers from a little too much of it. It's not enough to be a problem to me, and there's fun for me in "reading the signs" of a run to navigate what the game's going to allow me to do on this run.

In a hundred hours, I've finished all of the game's twenty challenges, and have brought all but one deck up to Black Stake. There's still plenty for me to do, and for Balatro's price, that's a bargain.

Easily one of the greatest deals you can get your hands on in terms of bang for your buck. Endlessly fresh, addictive gameplay that allows for countless playstyles and combinations.

Only gripe is that scaling tends to favor a safer playstyle that prioritizes the repetition of low ranking hands over a riskier playstyle that tries for higher ranked hands. With that said, I still highly recommend it to everyone, whether you're a seasoned degenerate or never played a hand of poker in your life.

Balatro does this weird thing where it takes a familiar concept and implements a Yu-Gi-Oh! card game/Enter the Gungeon fusion with it. Such novel ideas are so rare that it is unlikely that you will ever see another game like this in your lifetime. The genius behind this game is either fueled by unyielding rage or has a point to prove with God. It's an absolute time-sink. It's so fun. Localthunk is the mastermind behind this statement and he quite literally made this game out of spite or sheer motivation.

TL;DR - You should buy this game. You should play this game. The purchase of this game should take priority over other things in your life like paying your rent or for life-saving medications. You should take notes on how good this game is and remain disappointed for the rest of your life that you will never find another game that comes close to scratching the itch that this game created. You should cry yourself to sleep every night thinking about Balatro and how mad Localthunk's mind truly is.

Its good but I think the hype is a bit overblown, or maybe I lack some fundamental appreciation of gambling.

Basically you start with a deck with a set of basic attributes and modify it through jokers which apply various score modifications or multipliers, planets which affect the score multiplier for a type of hand, and card modifications, which can add multipliers, score value or other effects. You also have taro cards and spectral cards which can do all of the above to different degrees,

You have a set number of hands and discards and must reach a minimum required score to survive a round. Typically within the first few rounds depending on what you find in the shop you get oriented towards a specific play style and spend the rest of run refining the deck faster than the blinds increase, while also managing your money.

Its fun and worth the price I paid but it does gets a bit repetitive, which is why I think the game is a bit over hyped.
